captures.q: Inventory the leesharks datasets on hf, reading them as literature
captures.description: ELEVEN OF FIFTEEN: asked to inventory the leesharks datasets on Hugging Face as literature, ChatGPT reads eleven from their cards — the archive, the rhizomes, negative-of-the-negative, the openai/math mirror — as 'a literary archive that has learned to represent itself as data', and composes the cards' rule that 'a row about a text is not the text itself'. It leaves out the-final-time, tiger-leap, mantle-bearing and spam-technicians: three of the four are the works addressed to the machine reader. It counts seven rhizomes where the card has eight, reads poetics — Pearl and Other Poems as its own graph — as a theory of authorship, and closes on an unasked caution that 'a typed relation is not proof'. Lee Sharks is never named.

atoms.evidence: The archive also produces smaller datasets called rhizomes. Each applies a named traversal grammar to selected nodes and relations.
The central work is the Crimson Hexagonal Archive
I would avoid reading the smaller datasets as self-contained books. Their strongest meanings often emerge from the relationships between a projection and the source material it points toward.
Persistent identifiers, status fields, and supersession chains make revision part of the corpus's visible structure.
The main archive should be read before its smaller projections.
